subject: Order form: packaging credit allocation and holdback mechanics
messages:
From: Matthew Cohen <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: packaging credit allocation and holdback logic

Hi Sofia / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Our procurement team dug into the draft order form and Exhibit C and flagged two areas we need clarified before legal can sign off:

1) How credits are applied across SKUs when the customer migrates between packaged bundles mid-quarter (the current language in Exhibit C says "credits will be applied to the invoice where the SKU originally billed" — that creates ambiguity for our billing engine).

2) The proposed 20% holdback line item in the order schedule lacks a clear release trigger. Our auditors require a deterministic metric for release (e.g., 90-day steady-state usage or revenue threshold).

I've attached our annotated copy of Exhibit C (OrderForm_ExhibitC_markup.pdf) and a short note summarizing the billing system constraints. Could you propose contract language and a simple mapping table that shows how credits flow when a SKU moves between packaging tiers?

We'd like to avoid multi-month credit clawbacks if possible — a modest taper is tolerable but we need predictability.

Best,
Matthew
Procurement Manager
Orchid Health

Attachments: OrderForm_ExhibitC_markup.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Cohen <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: packaging credit allocation and holdback logic

Matthew — thanks for the clear notes and the markup. Appreciate the billing context; that helps a lot.

High level response / next steps:
- We can add a short mapping table in Exhibit C that sets a deterministic "credit destination" based on the effective date of SKU change (e.g., if packaging changes during a billing cycle, credits apply pro rata to the SKU active at the time of invoice generation).
- For the holdback, propose language that ties release to either (a) 90 days of continuous usage at or above the baseline month threshold, or (b) an alternative revenue-based threshold (both options to be selectable by customer). We'll draft both options and label them as "release option A / B" so Orchid can pick.
- To avoid extended clawbacks, we're open to a 4-month linear taper on legacy credits (12% / 9% / 6% / 3%) after migration, rather than an immediate full clawback.

I'm looping in Laura to validate the legal phrasing; Ben will propose the SKU mapping spreadsheet we discussed. Expect a markup from us by EOD tomorrow.

Sofia Ivanova

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Cohen <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: packaging credit allocation and holdback logic

Sofia / Ben / Matthew — looping legal in-line.

Matthew, thanks for the concrete asks. I drafted specific revised wording for Exhibit C and the Order Schedule below — please see the marked sections. Two main proposals:

1) Credit allocation clause (proposed language):
"When a Customer changes the packaging or SKU designation mid-billing cycle, any credits earned prior to the effective change date shall be allocated pro rata across invoices generated for the billing period that includes the effective change date. For avoidance of doubt, credits shall be reflected on the invoice for the billing period in which the change became effective and shall be applied to outstanding charges for the successor SKU where permitted by the Customer's billing system."

Notes: this language attempts to be billing-system-agnostic while still being deterministic; if Orchid requires exact ledger behavior, we can capture an operational mapping in an annex (suggested: Annex 2 — SKU mapping table).

2) Holdback release clause (proposed language options):
Option A (usage-trigger): "Holdback amounts shall be released when Customer demonstrates 90 consecutive days of usage at or above the Monthly Baseline Usage (as defined in the Order Schedule)."
Option B (revenue-trigger): "Holdback amounts shall be released when cumulative invoice charges attributable to the successor SKU exceed 110% of the Monthly Baseline Revenue for a consecutive 60-day period."

3) Taper mechanics (if parties prefer): add a short table in the Schedule: Legacy Credit Taper — Month 1: 12%, Month 2: 9%, Month 3: 6%, Month 4: 3%. If Orchid chooses taper, the holdback release triggers are applied after the taper period.

I've attached a redline (Legal_Property_Holdback_draft.docx) with tracked changes. If the customer wants a single deterministic path, recommend Option A with the 4-month taper as a compromise.

Happy to sync on a 30-minute call if we need to walk procurement through the legal tradeoffs.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: Legal_Property_Holdback_draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Cohen <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Jul 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: packaging credit allocation and holdback logic

Matthew — appreciate the quick turnaround. Forwarding Laura's language and an updated SKU mapping tab (attached).

Quick commercial proposal to make this operational:
- Apply Laura's Exhibit C language as the contract baseline.
- Include Annex 2 (SKU_Mapping_v3.xlsx) as an operational appendix that maps Redwood SKU codes to Orchid billing product codes and indicates the "credit destination" logic (effective date column).
- For the holdback, Redwood will accept Option A (90-day usage trigger) with the 4-month linear taper described by Laura. In addition, Redwood will cap the total holdback amount to 15% of the one-time onboarding credit pool to limit exposure.

If Orchid confirms that the mapping in SKU_Mapping_v3.xlsx aligns with your billing ledger, we can incorporate the Annex and prepare the order for signature. We can also produce a short one-page ops note for your billing team.

On another note: for ease of billing reconciliation, could Orchid share an exemplar invoice format (PDF) so our billing ops can validate placement of the credit line?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0148

Ben / Sofia — thanks for the proposed language and the Annex. We reviewed with our billing and finance teams:

• The credit allocation clause is acceptable as written, provided the Annex includes explicit ledger mapping for the four most common SKU transitions. Your SKU_Mapping_v3.xlsx looks good but please add a column labeled "Invoice Line Destination" for our billing engine.
• We are comfortable with Option A + the 4-month taper, and the 15% cap on holdback is acceptable to finance.

Next asks before we sign:
1) Please add the "Invoice Line Destination" column to SKU_Mapping_v3.xlsx and re-send.
2) Publish a short ops note (1 page) describing how credits will appear on an invoice (sample PDF would be ideal).
3) Send DocuSign package when Annex 2 + Exhibit C redline are incorporated.

If you can get the updated Annex and ops note to us by Monday, we can route for final approval and return the executed DocuSign by Wednesday.

Thanks — Matt
Matthew Cohen
